skill.name: hyperframes-registry
skill.description: Install HyperFrames registry blocks and components, then wire them into compositions. It covers the add command, install paths, block embedding, component merging, registry discovery, and contribution templates.
skill.summary: Install, discover, wire, and author HyperFrames registry items.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential access, or hidden exfiltration was found. Most static findings are Markdown false positives; confirmed risks are explicit CLI commands, remote registry access, CDN dependencies, and preview publishing.

remediation.suggestion: State that hyperframes, curl, npx, git, and gh commands require user approval and should run only in the intended project directory.
Pin registry refs when possible, add integrity checks, or vendor critical scripts. Document every external domain used by examples.

remediation.issue: Preview publishing can expose project content
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before running hyperframes publish and explain which files or assets may be uploaded.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames users need reliable steps for adding reusable animation blocks and components. This skill guides registry discovery, installation, wiring, and contribution workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install blocks and components with hyperframes add.
Shows default and configurable install paths in hyperframes.json.
Provides block wiring guidance for index.html composition attributes.
Describes how to merge component HTML, CSS, and script snippets.
Lists registry discovery methods and item metadata fields.
Provides templates and validation steps for new registry items.
limitations: Does not verify the safety of third-party registry content.
Requires the HyperFrames CLI and project structure.
Uses external registry and CDN URLs in examples.
Does not replace review of generated HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

use_cases.title: Add an animation block
use_cases.description: Install a registry block and identify the host composition attributes needed for playback.

use_cases.title: Wire reusable effects
use_cases.description: Merge a component snippet into an existing composition without losing timeline control.

use_cases.title: Contribute a registry item
use_cases.description: Follow the scaffold, validation, preview, and pull request workflow for a new item.

prompt_templates.title: Install a block
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-registry to add the data-chart block and show where to wire it in index.html.

prompt_templates.title: Add a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-registry to install shimmer-sweep and explain how to merge its markup, styles, and timeline calls.

prompt_templates.title: Compare registry options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-registry to find blocks for a data visualization segment. Compare types, duration, and wiring needs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a contribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-registry to scaffold a new transition block, create its manifest, validate it, and prepare a PR checklist.

output_examples.input: Add data-chart to my video project.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies it as a block, installs it through the HyperFrames CLI, and explains the host composition attributes to set.

output_examples.input: I need a reusable shimmer effect.
output_examples.output: The skill selects a component workflow, points to the installed snippet, and describes how to merge markup, styles, and timeline calls.

output_examples.input: I want to publish a new registry block.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines clarification, scaffold, validation, preview, and pull request steps, including user confirmation before publishing.

best_practices: Confirm before running commands that modify files or contact external services.
Review installed HTML, CSS, and JavaScript before merging into a project.
Use unique prefixes for IDs to avoid composition collisions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste component scripts from untrusted registry items without review.
Do not publish previews or run authenticated commands without explicit user approval.
Do not hand-author a block when an existing registry item matches the need.

faq.question: What does this skill install?
faq.answer: It guides HyperFrames blocks and components from the registry. The CLI performs the actual file changes.

faq.question: Can it browse the live registry?
faq.answer: It explains registry discovery through public GitHub and HyperFrames CLI commands.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands should run only after user confirmation in the active workspace.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Claude Code, and Codex as supported tools.

faq.question: What is the difference between blocks and components?
faq.answer: Blocks are standalone compositions. Components are snippets merged into an existing composition.

faq.question: Is third-party content reviewed?
faq.answer: The skill does not verify every registry item. Review installed files before use.
